groundings.excerpt:
14: For a type-\(A_{n-1}\) bigrassmannian permutation \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), Theorem 5.4 supplies two generating sets for the ideal \(J_v\). The authors conjecture:
15: 
16: > **Conjecture.** The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem 5.4 are both minimal.
17: 
18: Here, if \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), the parameters are
19: 
20: \[
21: a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\qquad b=\min(i,j).
22: \]
23: 
24: Theorem 5.4 gives the two sets
25: 
26: \[
27: \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}
28: \]
29: 
30: and
31: 
32: \[
33: \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}.
34: \]
35: 
36: Each contains
37: 
38: \[
39: \binom{a+b}{a}
40: \]
41: 
42: generators. “Minimal” means that no proper subset still generates \(J_v\).

claims.text: The truncated Pieri presentation has \(431\) Schur-basis columns and \(2130\) Pieri rows. Complementary-column eliminations for both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) use only unit pivots and leave no residual relation; the computed quotient is \(\mathbb Z^{10}\), with either family giving a basis. [artifact 0b05e147fd3b8f028a0683ee0de19704b04f214954cc0d8c387547f8371d7299]

Assuming the standard identification \(A_+J_v=\sum_{k=1}^{6}h_kJ_v\) and that these two families generate \(J_v\), the computation implies both families are irredundant generators of \(J_v\), by graded Nakayama.
